text: Approach: Objectives and Expected OutcomesObjectives:• Investigate the diagnostic accuracy and reliability of computer vision-based AI in skin cancer detectioncompared to human experts [2][1].• Analyze the legal and ethical issues associated with liability, data bias, and the reduction of humaninvolvement in critical decision-making [2][3].• Propose ethical and regulatory guidelines for the safe and effective implementation of AI in dermatology.Expected Outcomes:• Comprehensive insights into the technical and ethical barriers of AI in dermatology.• Recommendations for addressing these barriers, including alternative regulatory models and ethicaloversight mechanisms.• A framework that integrates AI into clinical workflows without undermining patient safety and trust.

text: Computer vision AI models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved impressiveaccuracy in image-based diagnostics, including skin cancer detection. Studies like Esteva et al. (2017)[2]have shown these models outperforming dermatologists in certain scenarios. However, despite their technicalprowess, the deployment of such systems is limited due to legal ambiguities, including unclear fault attributionin case of errors, and ethical concerns such as data privacy and algorithmic bias [3].The literature also highlights the growing demand for frameworks that ensure both accountability and patienttrust in AI-driven healthcare. Existing studies have examined these issues in other medical domains but rarelyfocus on dermatology, creating a gap this research seeks to address [4][1]
